title: Deep clone the object passed to transformData

comments.body:
Indeed every data we pass to user functions should be cloned. An easy and performant cloning mechanism is JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()).

Other cloning method are really big with a lot of cases. Since we know it's pure parsed JSON then we should be safe with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()).

Spots:
- https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/6ce160b7505a21fd16b3207b8f37b658c2e120b5/src/components/Template.js#L100
- https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/6ce160b7505a21fd16b3207b8f37b658c2e120b5/src/components/Template.js#L71
- https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/6ce160b7505a21fd16b3207b8f37b658c2e120b5/src/components/Template.js#L75

> I'm opening this issue since I've been affected in my currentRefinedValues implementation, I modified the name value for the display and ended up screwing up my onClick handler which was using it.

Even if we should clone data, I wonder how this can happen

True, but should we really have to worry about this?
I'm pretty sure that's something we'll miss in code reviews.
Let's see once you submit the PR (for currentRefinedValues), it will be easier to discuss there indeed. The issue you brought still need to be taken care of that's for sure
